questions.q: What is friction? What factors affect it, and what are its types?
answer: Friction is the force that opposes the relative motion between two surfaces in contact, always acting in the direction opposite to motion.

answer.text: It is caused by the tiny irregularities on the surfaces interlocking with one another. Friction is greater when the surfaces are rougher and when they are pressed together more firmly, for example by a heavier weight.

Static friction acts before motion begins and is the largest. Sliding friction acts when one surface slides over another. Rolling friction acts when one body rolls over another and is the smallest. Thus rolling friction is less than sliding friction, which is less than static friction.

answer: This is why it is easier to roll a heavy object than to drag it.

questions.q: Why is friction called both a friend and a foe, and how can it be reduced?

answer.text: Friction makes many everyday actions possible. It lets us walk without slipping, write with a pen, hold and grip objects, and stop vehicles using brakes. Without friction we could neither move nor hold anything.
Friction also causes the wear and tear of machine parts and shoe soles, and produces heat, wasting energy.

Friction can be reduced by using lubricants such as oil and grease, by polishing surfaces, and by using ball bearings, which change sliding into rolling. Objects moving through fluids face fluid friction, or drag, which is reduced by giving them a streamlined shape, as seen in birds, fish and aeroplanes.
